title: Tidy Data Extraction from Seurat Objects
text: Seurat’s FetchData() standard way pull data Seurat object custom plotting downstream analysis. works, rough edges: Returns data.frame cell barcodes rownames, column Mixes expression data, embeddings, metadata one flat call control layer (counts vs normalised) extract Returns wide format features, requires manual pivoting tidy workflows BadranSeq provides two focused alternatives: return tibbles cell_id explicit column.

title: Tidy Data Extraction from Seurat Objects
text: Seurat::FetchData() returns simple request — UMAP coordinates plus gene: Cell barcodes trapped rownames. Expression embeddings mingled. way request specific layer. title: Tidy Data Extraction from Seurat Objects
text: Combine expression UMAP coordinates fully self-contained plotting tibble:  Compare equivalent using FetchData():  produce plot, fetch_feature_data() gives tidy tibble feature name data, column name — making straightforward facet across multiple genes without reshaping.
code: cd3d <- fetch_feature_data(   pbmc3k,   features = "CD3D",   reductions = "umap",   metadata = FALSE )  ggplot(cd3d, aes(x = UMAP1, y = UMAP2, colour = data)) +   geom_point(size = 0.5) +   scale_colour_viridis_c(option = "B", direction = -1) +   theme_minimal() +   labs(colour = "CD3D") fd <- Seurat::FetchData(pbmc3k, vars = c("umap_1", "umap_2", "CD3D"))  ggplot(fd, aes(x = umap_1, y = umap_2, colour = CD3D)) +   geom_point(size = 0.5) +   scale_colour_viridis_c(option = "B", direction = -1) +   theme_minimal()

title: Publication-Ready Single-Cell Visualisation
text: Seurat’s plotting functions designed exploration. Getting publication quality typically requires layering ggplot2 theme adjustments, adding cell borders, repositioning legends, reformatting axis labels — boilerplate repeated across every figure manuscript. BadranSeq wraps small set functions opinionated defaults: cell borders , cluster labels , clean white theme, legend bottom. goal plot looks good paper without additional customisation.

title: Publication-Ready Single-Cell Visualisation
text: quickest way see difference — data plotted Seurat::DimPlot() BadranSeq::do_UmapPlot():  BadranSeq adds cell borders, boxed cluster labels, clean theme automatically. theme() calls needed.
code: p1 <- Seurat::DimPlot(pbmc3k, reduction = "umap") +   ggtitle("Seurat::DimPlot()")  p2 <- do_UmapPlot(pbmc3k) +   ggtitle("BadranSeq::do_UmapPlot()")  p1 + p2

title: Publication-Ready Single-Cell Visualisation
text: BadranSeq’s signature visualisation feature. pass split., panel shows: grey silhouette cells (spatial context) Black borders cells Coloured cells current split category preserves spatial layout across panels, making easy see subpopulation sits relative full dataset. First, add synthetic condition demonstrate: Now compare Seurat’s default split BadranSeq’s silhouette approach:   Seurat version, panel shows cells — lose sense cells sit overall structure. BadranSeq’s version, grey background preserves context: can immediately see clusters enriched condition. silhouette approach works grouping:
code: set.seed(42) pbmc3k$condition <- sample(   c("Control", "Treatment"),   ncol(pbmc3k),   replace = TRUE ) p1 <- Seurat::DimPlot(pbmc3k, reduction = "umap", split.by = "condition") +   ggtitle("Seurat::DimPlot(split.by)")  p1 do_UmapPlot(pbmc3k, split.by = "condition") do_UmapPlot(pbmc3k, group.by = "seurat_annotations", split.by = "condition")

title: Publication-Ready Single-Cell Visualisation
text: BadranSeq provides two violin plot functions built fetch_feature_data(): do_StatsViolinPlot() — wraps ggstatsplot::ggbetweenstats() -group comparisons built-statistical testing. do_ViolinPlot() — pure ggplot2 violin boxplot overlay, jittered points, centrality markers (statistical testing). primary function do_StatsViolinPlot(). want aesthetic without statistics, use do_ViolinPlot() set pairwise.display = "none" do_StatsViolinPlot().

title: Publication-Ready Single-Cell Visualisation
text: do_StatsViolinPlot() runs nonparametric omnibus test (Kruskal–Wallis) pairwise comparisons (Dunn’s test) default, annotating plot p-values:  nine annotation groups, pairwise brackets overwhelm figure. pairwise.display argument controls :
code: do_StatsViolinPlot(pbmc3k, features = "CD3D",                    group.by = "seurat_annotations",                    pairwise.display = "none") ## Warning: ✖ Number of labels is greater than default palette color count. ## ℹ Select another color `palette` (and/or `package`). ## Scale for colour is already present. ## Adding another scale for colour, which will replace the existing scale.

title: Publication-Ready Single-Cell Visualisation
text: Setting pairwise.display = "none" keeps subtitle showing overall test statistic removing bracket annotations — useful publication figures brackets overlap.

title: Publication-Ready Single-Cell Visualisation
text: Often want compare cell types — perhaps biologically relevant. group.levels argument filters grouping variable specified subset statistical test run, test performed groups care . fewer groups, pairwise brackets become readable :  cleaner subsetting Seurat object manually avoids need drop unused factor levels.
code: do_StatsViolinPlot(pbmc3k, features = "CD3D",                    group.by = "seurat_annotations",                    group.levels = c("Naive CD4 T", "Memory CD4 T", "CD8 T")) ## Scale for colour is already present. ## Adding another scale for colour, which will replace the existing scale.

title: Publication-Ready Single-Cell Visualisation
text: default nonparametric test appropriate scRNA-seq data, can switch parametric (ANOVA / t-test), robust, Bayesian tests via type argument:
code: do_StatsViolinPlot(pbmc3k, features = "CD3D",                    group.by = "seurat_annotations",                    group.levels = c("Naive CD4 T", "Memory CD4 T", "CD8 T"),                    type = "parametric") ## Scale for colour is already present. ## Adding another scale for colour, which will replace the existing scale.

text: BadranSeq R package produces publication-ready figures Seurat objects without additional styling. Built native ggplot2, closes gap exploratory analysis manuscript-quality visualisation Seurat’s defaults leave open.

title: Make transcriptomic analyses more pleasant
text: Seurat’s plotting functions designed exploration, publication. Every project ends boilerplate: computing formatting PCA variance labels, adding cell borders, styling themes, building split-panel comparisons preserve spatial context, wiring statistical annotations violin plots. work repeated across every analysis, every manuscript, every lab.

title: Make transcriptomic analyses more pleasant
text: figures generated default settings — theme adjustments, manual annotations.  BadranSeq adds cell borders, boxed cluster labels, vivid colour palette, clean theme — one function call.
code: library(BadranSeq) library(Seurat) library(ggplot2) library(patchwork) data(pbmc3k)  p1 <- DimPlot(pbmc3k, reduction = "umap") + ggtitle("Seurat::DimPlot()") p2 <- do_UmapPlot(pbmc3k) + ggtitle("BadranSeq::do_UmapPlot()") p1 + p2

BadranSeq differs providing lighter-weight native ggplot2 implementation additional features (PCA variance labels, statistical violin plots, interactive cell selection).

title: BadranSeq 1.0.0
text: do_DimPlot() provides unified entry point dimensionality reduction plots, routing specialised handlers based reduction argument. do_UmapPlot() produces publication-ready UMAP plots cell borders, boxed cluster labels, clean theme box. do_PcaPlot() adds automatic variance-explained labels PCA axes, formatted “PC1 (X.X%)”. do_FeaturePlot() overlays gene expression embeddings using viridis colour scale cells ordered expression. EnhancedElbowPlot() extends Seurat’s elbow plot variance percentage axis optional visual cutoff line. Split-panel silhouette feature: split.used, panel shows coloured cells current category grey silhouette cells, preserving spatial context across panels. do_StatsViolinPlot() creates statistical violin plots via ggstatsplot::ggbetweenstats() Seurat-aware data extraction, automatic colour generation, nonparametric testing (Kruskal–Wallis + Dunn’s) default. group.levels argument allows comparing subset groups without manually subsetting Seurat object. pairwise.display argument controls bracket visibility. do_ViolinPlot() creates descriptive violin plots boxplot overlay, jittered raw data points, centrality markers (median/mean diamond numeric label). Pure ggplot2, statistical testing. do_SankeyPlot() creates Sankey (alluvial) diagrams showing relationship 2–3 categorical metadata variables Seurat object. stratum labelled coloured; flows connect cells across variables. Powered ggalluvial.

title: BadranSeq 1.0.0
text: fetch_cell_data() extracts cell-level data Seurat objects tidy tibble one row per cell. Supports optional embeddings metadata selection. expression data included. fetch_feature_data() extracts feature expression data tidy tibble one row per cell per feature. Expression values one column per requested layer (features long, layers wide). Supports explicit assay layer selection, optional embeddings, optional metadata. functions replace Seurat::FetchData() cleaner interface: cell_id column (rownames), tibble output, explicit control data returned. get_pca_variance() returns data.frame variance explained cumulative variance per principal component.

title: BadranSeq 1.0.0
text: theme_badranseq() provides consistent publication-ready ggplot2 theme white background, grids, bold titles, legend bottom. generate_badranseq_colors() generates vivid, slightly darkened colours using colorspace Dark 3 qualitative palette.
